# II. SES mediation and school allocation

```{=latex}
\label{app-ses}
```

School-level and individual contrasts use the same fitted models. The notation below records the accounting identities used to construct the reported estimates.


With $\delta$ denoting the school-rank difference accompanying a 1-unit individual rank difference, define
$$
I_W=\sum_k a_{Wk}b_{Wk},\quad I_B=\sum_k a_{Bk}b_{Bk},\quad
I_S=(1-\delta)I_W+\delta I_B.
$$
The sorting increment is $I_S-I_W=\delta(I_B-I_W)$. Individual contributions are
$I_{S,k}=(1-\delta)a_{Wk}b_{Wk}+\delta a_{Bk}b_{Bk}$.
The remaining component is $D=(1-\delta)c'_W+\delta c'_B$, and the total is $T=D+I_S$.

The within-school total contribution is $G_W=(1-\delta)(c'_W+I_W)$; the between-school contribution is $G_B=\delta(c'_B+I_B)$. Their skills components are $K_W=(1-\delta)I_W$ and $K_B=\delta I_B$. Thus $G_W+G_B=T$ and $K_W+K_B=I_S$. These are contributions to the same individual-rank contrast, not variance components.

# III. Skill equalization

```{=latex}
\label{app-equal}
```

Let $d_{ik}$ denote the expected change in recipient $i$'s skill $k$ and $\bar d_{jk}$ its weighted school mean. The fitted change in reading is
$$
\Delta\widehat Y_{ij}=\sum_k\{b_{Wk}(d_{ik}-\bar d_{jk})+b_{Bk}\bar d_{jk}\}.
$$
The reduction in the reading gap equals the weighted mean recipient gain minus the weighted mean reference-group gain. School membership remains fixed.
